title: Turn-of-the-candle intraday anomaly in Bitcoin returns
economic_hypothesis: Exchange candle boundaries are a coordination device for order flow. A measurable, recurring drift appears around the turn of the candle, which is claimed to be statistically and economically significant and to survive an out-of-sample test.
market: Bitcoin spot (multiple venues in the source, including Bitfinex)
entry_rules: PARTIAL: the anomaly is defined as returns around the turn of the candle; the source does not readably state a tradable entry rule at the level read.
parameters: The candle-turn window (source uses venue-relative timing); no thresholds, no sizing.
claimed_period: in-sample historical sample plus an out-of-sample window January-August 2022 (Bitfinex)
claimed_metrics: positive returns of about 0.58 bps per minute around the candle turn, described as statistically and economically significant
external_results: Peer-reviewed anomaly paper with an explicit out-of-sample test; unusually good for this registry.
counter_evidence: 0.58 bps per minute is an order of magnitude below the project's 23.791 bps round-trip cost floor; the whole anomaly is smaller than one side of the trade.
The anomaly is tied to exchange-specific candle timing, so its magnitude is sensitive to which venue's clock defines the turn - a fidelity trap for replication.
No cost model, no net-of-cost result, and no statement about what share of the 0.58 bps survives a market-order entry.
ambiguities: Whether the return is capturable at all with a market order at the boundary is untested by the source.
The exact window length and pre/post split are not established at the level read.
replication_difficulty: MEDIUM methodologically, but the result is economically unusable.
evidence_quality: HIGH as an anomaly, LOW as an opportunity.
selection_note: Rejected for the same reason OPP-0005 is: the gross effect per trade is a fraction of the project's cost floor. Recorded so the rejection is auditable rather than implicit.
